features.name: __proto__
features.description: The __proto__ property of objects partially exposes the prototype of an object.

features.name: ::before and ::after
features.description: The ::before and ::after CSS pseudo-elements select inline boxes preceding and following an element. They are often used with the content property to generate cosmetic content.

features.name: ::first-letter
features.description: The ::first-letter CSS pseudo-element selects the first letter in an element for styling.

features.name: ::first-line
features.description: The ::first-line CSS pseudo-element selects the first line of text in an element for styling.

features.name: :empty
features.description: The :empty CSS pseudo-class matches elements without child elements.

features.name: :lang()
features.description: The :lang() CSS functional pseudo-class matches elements based on their content language.

features.name: :nth-child()
features.description: The :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() CSS functional pseudo-classes match elements based on their index within a list of elements. The :first-child and :last-child pseudo-classes match the first and last element in a list, and the :only-child pseudo-class matches an element with no siblings.

features.name: :nth-of-type() pseudo-classes
features.description: The :nth-of-type() and :nth-last-of-type() CSS functional pseudo-classes match elements based on their position among siblings of the same type. The :first-of-type, :last-of-type, and :only-of-type pseudo-classes match the first, last, and only elements of its type.

features.name: :root
features.description: The :root pseudo-class matches the root element of the document, usually the <html> element.

features.name: :target
features.description: The :target CSS pseudo-class matches the element with an ID matching the URL fragment.

features.name: @charset
features.description: The @charset CSS at-rule specifies the character encoding of an external style sheet.

features.name: @import
features.description: The @import CSS at-rule loads styles from another stylesheet.

features.name: @namespace
features.description: The @namespace CSS rule sets a default namespace or namespace prefix. Namespace prefixes allow CSS selectors to distinguish elements with the same name but different document types, such as the HTML <a> element and the SVG <a> element.

features.name: @supports (compatibility prefix)
features.description: The @supports (-webkit-transform-3d) CSS media query is a standardized compatibility alternative to @supports (transform-style).

features.name: <a>
features.description: The <a> element creates a hyperlink to any resource that's accessible via a URL, such as web pages, files, email addresses, or locations within the same page.

features.name: <abbr>
features.description: The <abbr> HTML element represents an abbreviation or acronym.

features.name: <address>
features.description: The <address> element represents contact information for a person or people, or for an organization.

features.name: <audio>
features.description: The <audio> element plays sound such as audio effects or music, optionally with controls provided by the browser.

features.name: <b>
features.description: The <b> HTML element draws reader's attention to text, styling text as bold by default.

features.name: <base>
features.description: The <base> element sets the base URL (the URL that relative URLs are relative to) for all relative URLs in the document.

features.name: <bdo>
features.description: The <bdo> element overrides the directionality of text, so that the text within is rendered in a different direction than the surrounding text.

features.name: <blockquote>
features.description: The <blockquote> element represents an extended quotation, styling contents as an indented block by default.

features.name: <body>
features.description: The <body> element represents the content of an HTML document.

The
element produces line breaks in text.

features.name: <button>
features.description: The <button> HTML element represents a button that triggers some action, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog, styled as a labeled rectangular box by default.

features.name: <canvas>
features.description: The <canvas> HTML element is a space to draw graphics in, using the 2D canvas API, WebGL, or WebGPU.

features.name: <cite>
features.description: The <cite> element represents the title of a quoted, referenced, or mentioned creative work, such as a film or book.

features.name: <code>
features.description: The <code> element displays its contents as a fragment of computer code.

features.name: <del>
features.description: The <del> element represents a range of text that has been deleted from a document, styling text as strikethrough by default.

features.name: <div>
features.description: The <div> HTML element is the generic container for content.

features.name: <em>
features.description: The <em> HTML element emphasizes or stresses the content, styling text as italic by default.

features.name: <embed>
features.description: The <embed> element represents an external resource such as a PDF or SVG document. It was historically used for plugins such as Shockwave Flash.

features.name: <fieldset> and <legend>
features.description: The <fieldset> and <legend> elements group several form control elements within a web form.

features.name: <form>
features.description: The <form> element contains interactive controls for submitting information.

features.name: <h1> through <h6>
features.description: The <h1> through <h6> HTML elements represent six levels of section headings, in order of decreasing importance.

features.name: <head>
features.description: The <head> element contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, such as the title, <script> and <style> elements, and <meta> elements.

features.name: <hr>
features.description: The <hr> element represents a thematic break between paragraphs, often shown as a horizontal rule.

features.name: <html>
features.description: The <html> element represents the top-level of an HTML document and is referred to as the root element.

features.name: <i>
features.description: The <i> HTML element identifies idiomatic content, styling text as italic by default.

features.name: <iframe>
features.description: The <iframe> element embeds another HTML page into the current page.
The element adds an image into the document.

features.name: <input type="button">
features.description: The <input type="button"> HTML element represents a button that triggers some action, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog, styled as a labeled rectangular box by default. Not to be confused with the <button> element, which contains HTML content.

features.name: <input type="checkbox">
features.description: The <input type="checkbox"> HTML element represents a tickable box with two states, checked and unchecked.

features.name: <input type="file" multiple>
features.description: The <input type="file" multiple> HTML element shows a file picker from which users can choose one or more files to upload with a form.

features.name: <input type="file">
features.description: The <input type="file"> HTML element shows a file picker from which users can choose a file to upload with the form.

features.name: <input type="hidden">
features.description: The <input type="hidden"> HTML element represents a form field that is not shown visually but is still included in the form submission.

features.name: <input type="image">
features.description: The <input type="image"> HTML element is an image that can be used to submit a form, like the <input type="submit"> element.

features.name: <input type="password">
features.description: The <input type="password"> HTML element represents a field for users to enter a password. The password is hidden from view, typically replaced by dots or asterisks.

features.name: <input type="radio">
features.description: The <input type="radio"> HTML element represents one button in a group such that only one can be chosen at a time.

features.name: <input type="reset">
features.description: The <input type="reset"> HTML element represents a button that sets all form fields to their initial values.

features.name: <input type="submit">
features.description: The <input type="submit"> HTML element represents a button that triggers an action on its associated <form>, such as sending the form data to a server.

features.name: <input>
features.description: The <input type="text"> HTML element allows the user to enter information into a form. By default, an <input> element is a text input.

features.name: <ins>
features.description: The <ins> element represents a range of text that has been inserted into a document, styling text as underlined by default.

features.name: <kbd>
features.description: The <kbd> element represents textual user input, such as keyboard or voice input, styling text in monospaced type by default.

features.name: <label>
features.description: The <label> HTML element represents a caption for a form field.

features.name: <link>
features.description: The <link> element creates a relationship between the current document and an external resource, such as a stylesheet or favicon.

features.name: <menu>
features.description: The <menu> element represents an unordered list of action items (<li>), such as a toolbar. It is a semantic alternative to the <ul> element.

features.name: <meta>
features.description: The <meta> element represents metadata about the page used by the browser or search engines, including description, keywords, and character sets.

features.name: <object>
features.description: The <object> element represents an external resource such as a PDF or SVG document. It was historically used for plugins such as Shockwave Flash.

features.name: <ol>, <ul>, and <li>
features.description: The <ol>, <ul>, and <li> HTML elements represent ordered and unordered lists.

The

element represents a paragraph of text.

features.name: <pre>
features.description: The <pre> element represents a block element of preformatted text that is presented exactly as written, including all white space.

features.name: <q>
features.description: The <q> element represents a short inline quotation.

features.name: <s>
features.description: The <s> HTML element indicates text that is no longer relevant or accurate, styling text as strikethrough by default.

features.name: <samp>
features.description: The <samp> element represents a sample or quoted output from a computer program. Styled in a monospace font by default.

features.name: <script> and <noscript>
features.description: The <script> element contains or loads data or executable code. This is typically used to load JavaScript code. The <noscript> element represents alternative content to show when scripting is not allowed.

features.name: <select>
features.description: The <select> element provides a menu of options for a user to pick from, typically rendered as a dropdown list.

features.name: <small>
features.description: The <small> element represents side-comments and small print, like copyright and legal text, independent of its styled presentation. Styled in a reduced font size by default.

features.name: <source>
features.description: The <source> element sets a media resource for the <picture>, <video>, and <audio> elements.

features.name: <span>
features.description: The <span> HTML element is the generic inline container for content.

features.name: <strong>
features.description: The <strong> HTML element brings attention to the content, styling text as bold by default.

features.name: <style>
features.description: The <style> element embeds an inline CSS stylesheet in a document.

features.name: <sub> and <sup>
features.description: The <sub> and <sup> elements sets inline text to be displayed as subscript or superscript for solely typographical reasons.

features.name: <textarea>
features.description: The <textarea> element represents an editing control that allows users to enter multi-line, free-form, plain text.

features.name: <title>
features.description: The <title> element sets the title of the document and exposes it to users via the UI of the browser or app they're using and through assistive technology.

features.name: <u>
features.description: The <u> HTML element makes non-textual annotations, styling text as underlined by default.

features.name: <var>
features.description: The <var> element represents the name of a variable in a mathematical expression or a programming context.

features.name: <video>
features.description: The <video> element plays videos or movies, optionally with controls provided by the browser.

features.name: <wbr>
features.description: The <wbr> HTML element represents a word break opportunity, to explicitly mark a place within a word where a line might be broken.

features.name: 2D canvas
features.description: The CanvasRenderingContext2D API is the "2d" rendering context for the <canvas> element. It represents a flat, two-dimensional space for drawing graphics and animations.

features.name: Absolute positioning
features.description: The position: absolute CSS declaration removes an element from the normal flow and positions it relative to its containing block, which is often the root element, or closest positioned ancestor.

features.name: Accessor methods
features.description: The __defineGetter__() and __defineSetter__() methods of objects bind a function to a property, which is called on setting or reading the property.

features.name: Alerts
features.description: The window.alert(), window.confirm(), and window.prompt() methods open modal dialogs for notifying the user, asking for confirmation, or entering text.

features.name: arguments.callee
features.description: The callee property of the arguments variable in a non-strict function body's local scope is the function that arguments belongs to.

features.name: Array (initial support)
features.description: Arrays are ordered lists of JavaScript values.

features.name: Array iteration methods
features.description: Array iteration methods

features.name: Array splice()
features.description: The array splice() method changes an array in-place. You can use it to delete items, overwrite items, or insert items, starting from an index.

features.name: attr() (content only)
features.description: The attr() CSS function, in content property declarations, sets a ::before or ::after pseudo-element's content to the value of the specified HTML attribute.

features.name: autofocus
features.description: The autofocus HTML attribute gives focus to an element on page load.

features.name: background
features.description: The background CSS property is a shorthand that sets several background properties at once.

features.name: background-color
features.description: The background-color CSS property sets the fill color of an element, behind any content and background images or gradients.

features.name: background-image
features.description: The background-image CSS property sets the graphics to display behind the content of an element and in front of the background color. Graphics may be any combination of images or gradients.

features.name: BarProp
features.description: The visible property of the window.locationbar, window.menubar, window.personalbar, window.scrollbars, window.statusbar, and window.toolbar APIs historically represented the visibility of a browser user interface. For privacy reasons, it now represents whether the window is a pop-up.

features.name: BMP
features.description: The BMP image format is an uncompressed raster graphics file format. Also known as a bitmap.

features.name: Borders
features.description: The border CSS property sets the color, style, and width of the line around an element.

features.name: Change event
features.description: The change event for <input>, <select>, and <textarea> elements fires when the user modifies the element's value. Unlike the input event, the change event does not necessarily fire on every alteration to an element's value.

features.name: clip
features.description: The clip CSS property sets the visible area of an absolutely positioned element.

features.name: Color
features.description: The color CSS property sets the primary foreground color of an element, which is used for text, the default border color, and text decorations.

features.name: Console
features.description: The console API logs debugging messages to the browser development tools' console.

features.name: Content
features.description: The content CSS property sets the content inside of an element or pseudo-element, replacing the current value. It's often used with the ::before and ::after pseudo-elements to generate cosmetic content.

features.name: contenteditable
features.description: The contenteditable global HTML attribute allows the user to edit the content of an element, such as inserting or deleting text.

features.name: Cookies
features.description: The Set-Cookie HTTP header stores limited amounts of data that persist across request and response, creating shared state between the browser and server.

features.name: CORS
features.description: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing is an HTTP-header based mechanism that allows a server to indicate any origins (domain, scheme, or port) other than its own from which a browser should permit loading resources. Also known as CORS.

features.name: Counters (CSS)
features.description: The counter-reset and counter-increment CSS properties and the counter() and counters() functions automatically number headings or ordered list items.

features.name: currentColor
features.description: The currentColor CSS value allows you to reuse an element's computed text color for other properties.

features.name: Data URLs
features.description: Data URLs are URLs that start with the data: scheme and which directly contain data rather than point to remote resources.

features.name: Date
features.description: The Date object represents a single moment in time.

features.name: Description list
features.description: The <dl>, <dt>, and <dd> HTML elements represent a list of terms and their associated descriptions. Use a description list to create glossaries or similar list of key-value pairs.

features.name: Device media queries
features.description: The device-aspect-ratio, device-height, and device-width media features describe physical properties of the displaying output device.

features.name: Display
features.description: The display CSS property sets the display behavior of an element's box within its layout and sets the layout behavior for its child elements.

features.name: display: list-item
features.description: The display: list-item CSS declaration renders an element with the box layout of a <li> HTML element.

features.name: display: table
features.description: The display: table CSS declaration renders an element with the box layout of a <table> HTML element. Child elements may use equivalents to <table> internal elements such as display: table-row for <tr>.

features.name: DOM
features.description: The DOM (Document Object Model) API represents HTML and XML documents as trees of nodes. You can use the API to inspect and modify the structure and content of a document.

features.name: dominant-baseline
features.description: The dominant-baseline CSS property sets the specific baseline used to align an elements's text and inline-level contents.

features.name: Drag and Drop
features.description: The Drag and Drop API lets users drag and drop elements and external files such as images onto web pages. Developers can customize which elements can become draggable, the type of feedback the draggable elements produce, and the droppable elements.

features.name: em unit
features.description: The em CSS length unit is a font-relative length equal to the specified font size. In an element with a 2 inch font, 1em equals 2 inches.

features.name: Email, telephone, and URL <input> types
features.description: The <input type="email">, <input type="tel">, and <input type="url"> HTML elements represent email address, telephone number, and URL fields in a form.

features.name: escape() and unescape()
features.description: The escape() and unescape() built-in Javascript methods encode and unencode strings using percent encoding, where certain characters are replaced by hexadecimal escape sequences.

features.name: Events
features.description: The Event API and the addEventListener() method on objects that receive events (event targets) represent and handle significant things happening on a page. Many APIs fire events for a wide range of situations relating to those APIs, such as an image loading, a user clicking, or a value changing.

features.name: ex unit
features.description: The ex CSS length unit is a font-relative length equal to the used x-height of the first available font. X-height is often equal to the height of the lowercase x.

features.name: Fixed positioning
features.description: The position: fixed CSS declaration removes an element from the normal flow and positions it relative to the viewport or page.

features.name: float and clear
features.description: The float CSS property aligns an element to either side of its container, allowing text and inline elements to flow around it. The clear CSS property sets whether an element is moved below floating elements that proceed it.

features.name: Focus events
features.description: Focus events, such as focus and blur, fire when an element gets or loses focus.

features.name: Font shorthand
features.description: The font CSS property shorthand sets multiple font properties, including style, weight, size, and font family.

features.name: font-family
features.description: The font-family CSS property sets the desired font face for text, along with optional fallback font faces.

features.name: font-size
features.description: The font-size CSS property sets the text height.

features.name: font-style
features.description: The font-style CSS property sets the text style, with normal, italic, and oblique options.

features.name: font-variant
features.description: The font-variant CSS property is a shorthand for font-variant-alternates, font-variant-caps, font-variant-east-asian, font-variant-emoji, font-variant-ligatures, font-variant-numeric, and font-variant-position.

features.name: font-weight
features.description: The font-weight CSS property controls the thickness of a font. It is set explicitly with the keyword bold or a number, or relative to the inherited thickness with the keywords bolder or lighter.

features.name: Function caller and arguments
features.description: The caller and arguments properties of a non-strict mode Function object are the function that called it and the arguments it was called with. Not to be confused with the arguments variable in a function body's local scope.

features.name: Functions
features.description: Functions are series of statements that can be called and return a value. The function keyword (as in function () { }) and arrow (=>) expression create functions. The JavaScript functions protocol includes default and rest parameters and binding to this.

features.name: Geolocation API
features.description: The navigator.geolocation API requests the user's latitude, longitude, heading, and speed.

features.name: getYear() and setYear()
features.description: The getYear() and setYear() methods of Date objects get and set the year as an offset to 1900.

features.name: GIF
features.description: The GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) image format is a raster graphics file format with animation and lossless compression.

features.name: History
features.description: The window.history API manipulates the browser session history, from navigations to state management, in the tab or frame that the current page is loaded in.

features.name: HTML wrapper methods
features.description: JavaScript built-in methods such as, String.bold() and String.italics(), wrap strings in (often historic) HTML.

features.name: HTTP authentication
features.description: The Authorization and WWW-Authenticate headers authenticate a user with a server.

features.name: HTTP/1.1
features.description: HTTP/1.1 is a network protocol used by browsers and servers. It has been superseded by HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

features.name: Image maps
features.description: The <area> and <map> elements define a clickable area on an image.

features.name: inherit
features.description: The inherit keyword resets any CSS property to the computed value of that property from the parent element.

features.name: initial
features.description: The initial keyword resets any CSS property to its initial value as defined by the specification. For example, the initial value of the display property is inline, regardless of the element being styled. Not to be confused with revert, which resets to the user or browser default style.

features.name: input (event)
features.description: The input event fires when a form control changes or an element with the contenteditable attribute changes.

features.name: Input selectors
features.description: The :checked, :disabled, and :enabled CSS pseudo-classes match form elements based on their state.

features.name: JPEG
features.description: The JPEG image format is a raster graphics file format with lossy compression.

features.name: JSON
features.description: The JSON API provides static methods for parsing values from and converting values to JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), a serialization format for objects, arrays, numbers, strings, Boolean values, and null.

features.name: Keyboard events
features.description: The keydown and keyup events fire for each key press (or, with modifier keys, a combination of key presses) on a keyboard.

features.name: lang
features.description: The lang global HTML attribute defines the language of an element. It's used by assistive technology to correctly read the content, translation tools to select the origin language, and other applications.

features.name: Language
features.description: The navigator.language property is a string representing the preferred language of the user, usually the language of the browser UI. The navigator.languages property is an array of strings representing the user's preferred languages.

features.name: letter-spacing
features.description: The letter-spacing CSS property controls the amount of space between each letter in an element or block of text.

features.name: line-height
features.description: The line-height CSS property sets the spacing between text baselines, oriented to the horizontal or vertical writing mode.

features.name: List style
features.description: The list-style shorthand CSS property and the list-style-image, list-style-position, and list-style-type longhand properties set the position and appearance of a list item's marker.

features.name: localStorage and sessionStorage
features.description: The localStorage and sessionStorage APIs store data as key-value pairs. While localStorage persists across sessions, sessionStorage data is discarded when the page is closed.

features.name: Location
features.description: The location global object represents the current page's address. You can use it to get the parts of the address (such as location.hostname or location.pathname) or navigate to another URL.

features.name: margin
features.description: The margin CSS property sets space around an element. It is a shorthand for margin-top, margin-right, margin-bottom, and margin-left.

features.name: Math and numbers
features.description: The number type (and Number object) represents floating-point numbers, such as 42 or -4.201, while the Math API contains mathematical functions and constants. JavaScript can also represent boundless negative and positive values as Infinity or not-a-number as NaN (as in 0 * Infinity).

features.name: Media queries
features.description: The @media CSS rule conditionally applies styles based on the output device type, its capabilities, and the user's preferences. Media queries are composed of an optional media type such as screen or print, and one or more mandatory media features, such as prefers-reduced-animations.

features.name: Meta refresh
features.description: The <meta http-equiv="refresh"> HTML element and the equivalent Refresh HTTP header trigger a page reload or redirect. They apply only when the page is fully loaded, after other HTTP redirects or scripted redirects that might execute before the page is fully loaded.

features.name: Min and max width and height
features.description: The min-width, min-height, max-width, and max-height CSS properties set the minimum and maximum size of an element.

features.name: Mouse events
features.description: Mouse events, such as click, mousedown, or mousemove, fire when users interact with an input or pointing device such as a mouse, trackpad, or touchscreen.

features.name: Named colors
features.description: Some CSS color values can be referenced by name, such as red or limegreen. They stand in for specific RGB color values.

features.name: Navigator
features.description: The window.navigator API is a generic global object, under which many other, more interesting APIs are located. It doesn't do anything interesting on its own.

features.name: Object
features.description: Objects in JavaScript are collections of key-value pairs.

features.name: Online status
features.description: The navigator.onLine property is a boolean for whether the browser is connected to some network (though not necessarily the internet). The online and offline events fire when the connection state changes.

features.name: opacity
features.description: The opacity CSS property sets the transparency of an element.

features.name: Outlines
features.description: The outline-color, outline-style, and outline-width and outline-offset CSS properties style a line around an element, outside of the border.

features.name: padding
features.description: The padding CSS property sets space between an element's edge and its contents. It is a shorthand for padding-top, padding-right, padding-bottom, and padding-left.

features.name: Page transition events
features.description: The pageshow and pagehide transition events fire when a document loads or unloads due to a navigation, such as clicking on a link on a page or the back button in a browser.

features.name: Physical properties
features.description: The physical CSS properties, top, right, bottom, and left, set the inset position of an element relative to the corresponding side of a container determined by the element's position property.

features.name: pointer-events
features.description: The pointer-events CSS property sets whether a user can interact with an element using a mouse, touch, or other pointing input device.

features.name: Position
features.description: The position CSS property sets the origin position of an element to an element, the element's scrollport, or the viewport.

features.name: postMessage
features.description: The postMessage() global method sends cross-origin messages to windows and workers, including popups and iframes. Also known as cross-document messaging.

features.name: RegExp compile()
features.description: The compile() method of RegExp objects recompiles an existing regular expression object using a new pattern and flags.

features.name: RegExp static properties
features.description: The RegExp object has several static properties to access the input and results of the most-recent regular expression match.

features.name: Regular expressions
features.description: The RegExp object represents a regular expression, a notation for matching text patterns.

features.name: Relative positioning
features.description: The position: relative CSS declaration offsets the position of an element relative to its position in the normal flow.

features.name: rem
features.description: The rem CSS length unit is a font-relative length that is equal to the font size of the root HTML element which for most browsers is 16px.

features.name: Sandboxed iframes
features.description: The sandbox attribute for the <iframe> HTML element sets many security restrictions on the iframe, such as preventing form submissions or opening modal dialogs. Optional allow- values relax specific restrictions.

features.name: Screen
features.description: The window.screen property contains information about the screen of the output device that the referenced window is being rendered on.

features.name: scrollIntoView()
features.description: The scrollIntoView() method scrolls an element's ancestor containers such that the element is visible to the user.

features.name: Selectors (core)
features.description: CSS selectors match elements based on their type, attributes, and relationship to other elements. They define the specific elements to which a block of styles will be applied. This feature represents the oldest selectors of CSS.

features.name: Static positioning
features.description: The position: static CSS declaration positions an element in the normal flow. A statically positioned element ignores physical and logical properties such as top or inset-block-start.

features.name: String (initial support)
features.description: The string type (and String object) represents a sequence of characters.

features.name: String substr()
features.description: The substr() method of strings returns part of a string, starting from an index and ending a given number of characters after.

features.name: style (attribute)
features.description: The style global HTML attribute applies inline CSS styling declarations to individual elements.

features.name: SVG
features.description: The SVG image format, represented by the <svg> element, creates two-dimensional vector graphics with declarative or scripted interaction and animation.

features.name: System colors
features.description: The system color CSS keywords, such as ButtonBorder or LinkText, allow you to match default colors from the user agent.

features.name: tabindex
features.description: The tabindex HTML attribute make an element focusable, and sets the element's relative ordering for sequential focus navigation.

features.name: Tables
features.description: The <table> HTML element, with several related elements, represents tabular data in rows and columns of cells.

features.name: Text overflow
features.description: The text-overflow CSS property sets how hidden overflow content appears to users. The property can clip content, truncate content with an ellipsis (…), or truncate with a custom string.

features.name: Text stroke and fill  (compatibility prefixes)
features.description: The -webkit-text-stroke-width and -webkit-text-stroke-color CSS properties set the thickness and color of text outlines. The -webkit-text-fill-color sets the color within text character outlines. Both default to the text color.

features.name: text-align
features.description: The text-align CSS property sets the horizontal placement of the inner content of a block element.

features.name: text-decoration
features.description: The text-decoration CSS property sets the style and color of decorative lines including underline, overline, line-through, or a combination of lines.

features.name: text-indent
features.description: The text-indent CSS property sets the size of the empty space (indentation) at the beginning of lines in a text.

features.name: text-shadow
features.description: The text-shadow CSS property sets the position and styles of shadow on text.

features.name: text-transform
features.description: The text-transform CSS property sets text case and capitalization.

features.name: title (attribute)
features.description: The title global HTML attribute sets information about an element, such as a name or description. The value is typically shown as a tooltip that appears on mouse over. Since it's not often available to touch-only, keyboard-only, or assistive technology users, it's not a substitute for other text.

features.name: toGMTString()
features.description: The toGMTString() method of Date objects is an alias to the toUTCString() method.

features.name: User action pseudo-classes
features.description: The :active, :focus, and :hover CSS pseudo-classes match elements based on how users are interacting with them.

features.name: vertical-align
features.description: The vertical-align CSS property sets the vertical alignment of inline, inline-block, and table cell elements. It has no effect on block-level elements.

features.name: visibility
features.description: The visibility CSS property sets whether an element is shown. Invisible elements still affect the document layout.

features.name: white-space
features.description: The white-space CSS property sets how white space is collapsed and how lines wrap. It is a shorthand for white-space-collapse and text-wrap-mode.

features.name: Width and height
features.description: The width and height CSS properties set the preferred physical size of an element.

features.name: Window
features.description: The window global object represents a browser tab or iframe and its relationship to the document and other tabs. It's also a generic global object, under which many other APIs are located.

features.name: word-spacing
features.description: The word-spacing CSS property sets the amount of white space between words.

features.name: X-Frame-Options
features.description: The X-Frame-Options HTTP header limits where a document may be embedded in an iframe. The X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN header disallows embedding in another origin. The X-Frame-Options: DENY header disallows embedding in any context, regardless of origin.

features.name: XMLHttpRequest
features.description: The XMLHttpRequest API makes HTTP requests. It's the predecessor to fetch(). Also known as XHR.

features.name: XMLSerializer
features.description: The XMLSerializer API provides the serializeToString() method to construct an XML string representing a DOM tree.

features.name: XPath
features.description: The document.evaluate() method selects elements in an HTML or XML document based on an expression of XPath, a domain specific language for querying XML documents. Also known as XML Path Language.

features.name: XSLT
features.description: The XSLTProcessor API transforms XML documents into new XML or HTML documents, using XSLT stylesheets. You can use XSLT to convert data between different XML schemas or to convert XML data into web pages or PDF documents. Also known as Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations.

features.name: z-index
features.description: The z-index CSS property orders overlapping elements, with higher values appearing in front of or on top of lower values.

features.name: :default
features.description: The :default CSS pseudo-class matches the default element in a group of related form controls, such as checkboxes and radio buttons with the checked attribute.

features.name: :read-only and :read-write
features.description: The :read-only and :read-write CSS pseudo-classes match elements that are read-only or read-write, respectively. For example, :read-only matches <input> and <textarea> elements with the readonly attribute.

features.name: <article>
features.description: The <article> element represents self-contained content, which is intended to be independently distributable or reusable, such as a comment, a blog post, or news article.

features.name: <aside>
features.description: The <aside> element represents a portion of a document whose content is only indirectly related to the document's main content.

features.name: <figure> and <figcaption>
features.description: The <figure> and <figcaption> HTML elements represent an illustration, diagram, text, or other self-contained reference content, with an optional caption.

features.name: <header> and <footer>
features.description: The <header> and <footer> HTML elements represent content that precedes and follows the main page content, respectively.

features.name: <hgroup>
features.description: The <hgroup> element represents a heading and related content.

features.name: <input type="number">
features.description: The <input type="number"> HTML element represents numeric input data.

features.name: <input type="search">
features.description: The <input type="search"> HTML element represents a text field for search queries.

features.name: <mark>
features.description: The <mark> element represents text which is marked or highlighted for reference or notation purposes.

features.name: <nav>
features.description: The <nav> element represents a section of a page whose purpose is to provide navigation links, either within the current document or to other documents.

features.name: <ruby>
features.description: The <ruby> element produces small annotations that are rendered with its base text.

features.name: <section>
features.description: The <section> element is a generic standalone section of a document, which doesn't have a more specific semantic element to represent it.

features.name: Array.isArray()
features.description: The Array.isArray() static method checks whether a value is an array.

features.name: background-clip
features.description: The background-clip CSS property sets the extent of the background: the padding box, the content box, or the default border box.

features.name: background-origin
features.description: The background-origin CSS property sets the background starting position relative to the border and padding of an element.

features.name: background-size
features.description: The background-size CSS property scales or stretches a background based on the size of the element (with the contain and cover keywords), a length, or percentage.

features.name: border-radius
features.description: The border-radius CSS property rounds the corners of the border drawn around an element.

features.name: box-shadow
features.description: The box-shadow CSS property applies shadow effects around an element's frame. This can create drop shadow and inner shadow effects.

features.name: Channel messaging
features.description: Channel messaging communicates one-to-one between browsing contexts on the same origin, such as between <iframe> elements or two documents using a shared worker.

features.name: Dataset
features.description: The dataset API attaches and accesses custom data on elements, using either the dataset property of HTMLElement or attributes prefixed with data-.

features.name: Dedicated workers
features.description: The Worker() constructor runs a script in its own thread, which can send and receive messages with the script that created it. Also known as web workers.

features.name: execCommand()
features.description: The document.execCommand() method reads and writes from the clipboard and performs editing commands on editable text, such as changing the font name or style. Related methods check whether commands are supported, enabled, or applied.

features.name: Form validity pseudo-classes
features.description: The form validity CSS pseudo-classes match <form> elements based on the constraints of a form field, such as validity (:valid, :invalid, :in-range, :out-of-range) and necessity (:optional or :required).

features.name: getComputedStyle()
features.description: The getComputedStyle() global method returns an CSSStyleDeclaration object that represents all CSS declarations applied to a given element.

features.name: JavaScript (initial core language support)
features.description: JavaScript is a programming language that runs in browsers, usually through the <script> element. JavaScript has changed over many years. This feature represents the oldest language features, such as built-in objects, statements, and operators. Also known as ECMAScript.

features.name: matchMedia
features.description: The window.matchMedia() method checks whether a media query applies to the document.

features.name: resolution media query (compatibility prefixes)
features.description: The -webkit-device-pixel-ratio, -webkit-min-device-pixel-ratio, and -webkit-max-device-pixel-ratio CSS media queries are standardized compatibility alternatives to resolution media queries.

features.name: Selection
features.description: The Selection API controls and modifies user text selections within the page.

features.name: Server-sent events
features.description: The EventSource API creates a connection to a server and listens to a stream of events sent by the server.

features.name: setInterval
features.description: The setInterval() global function repeatedly executes provided code on a given delay, and the accompanying clearInterval() cancels the interval.

features.name: setTimeout()
features.description: The setTimeout() global function executes provided code after a given duration of time, and the accompanying clearTimeout() cancels the timer.

features.name: String trimLeft() and trimRight()
features.description: The trimLeft() and trimRight() methods of strings return a new string with whitespace removed from the beginning or end of the string. They're aliases for trimStart() and trimEnd().

features.name: Typed arrays (initial support)
features.description: Typed arrays are ordered lists of JavaScript values, where all values are of the same numerical type, such as 8-bit integers or 32-bit floating point numbers.

features.name: WebSockets
features.description: The WebSocket API opens a two-way communication channel between the user's browser and a server.

features.name: window.print()
features.description: The window.print() method opens the browser's print dialog.

features.name: word-break: break-word
features.description: The word-break: break-word CSS declaration sets word breaks to occur according to their customary rules.

features.name: <bdi>
features.description: The <bdi> element isolates text that may have a different text direction from its surrounding text. This prevents the browser's bidirectional text algorithm from affecting or being affected by the direction of the surrounding text.

features.name: <details>
features.description: The <details> element is a disclosure widget which can be expanded to reveal additional content. When closed, only the nested <summary> element is visible.

features.name: <dfn>
features.description: The <dfn> element marks a term to be defined, styling text as italic by default.

features.name: accesskey
features.description: The accesskey global HTML attribute gives a hint for generating a keyboard shortcut for the current element. The attribute value must consist of a single printable character.

features.name: AudioListener setPosition() and setOrientation()
features.description: The setPosition() and setOrientation() methods of the AudioListener API set the virtual position and orientation of a person relative to sound sources, to spatialize audio in a Web Audio context.

features.name: box-sizing
features.description: The box-sizing CSS property sets whether an element's width and height are calculated based on the content-box, which does not count the size of borders or padding, or border-box, which does count them.

features.name: cubic-bezier() easing
features.description: The cubic-bezier() CSS easing function interpolates along a smooth curve, creating animations and transitions with continuous changes in speed. The ease, ease-in, ease-out, and ease-in-out keyword values are presets for common Bézier curves.

features.name: hashchange
features.description: The hashchange event fires when the URL fragment identifier (the part of the URL starting with #) of the current page has changed.

features.name: SMIL SVG animations
features.description: The <animate>, <animateMotion>, and <animateTransform> SVG elements declaratively animate SVG elements. Also known as SMIL.

features.name: srcdoc
features.description: The srcdoc attribute for the <iframe> HTML element sets a string of HTML to embed in the document. The value of srcdoc overrides loading a document from the src attribute.

features.name: SVG filters
features.description: The <filter> SVG element applies custom effects such as color manipulation, blurring, or morphing to SVG elements.

features.name: Text tracks
features.description: The <track> element is used as a child of the media elements that lets you specify a timed text track to be displayed in parallel with the media element.

features.name: :scope (pseudo-class)
features.description: The :scope CSS pseudo-class matches the scoping root, for instance the element that querySelector() is called on, or the root of a DOM subtree specified with @scope.

features.name: <main>
features.description: The <main> element represents the dominant content of a document. It is commonly used together with <header> and <footer>.

features.name: <output>
features.description: The <output> element represents the result of a calculation, user action, or form entry.

features.name: <progress>
features.description: The <progress> element displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task, typically displayed as a progress bar.

features.name: <template>
features.description: The <template> HTML element holds HTML fragments which you can clone and insert into the document using JavaScript.

features.name: ANGLE_instanced_arrays WebGL extension
features.description: The ANGLE_instanced_arrays extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts draws the same object multiple times or groups of similar objects multiple times, if the group shares the same vertex data, primitive count and type.

features.name: background-position
features.description: The background-position CSS property offsets the initial position of background images relative to the background origin.

features.name: background-repeat
features.description: The background-repeat CSS property sets how a background image is tiled.

features.name: calc()
features.description: The calc() CSS function computes mathematical expressions such a calc(100%/3 - 1em).

features.name: ch unit
features.description: The ch CSS length unit is a font-relative length based on the width of the zero (0) character.

features.name: Composition events
features.description: The compositionstart, compositionupdate, and compositionend events fire when an input method editor adds characters that might not be commonly available on keyboards. Examples of these characters are emoji, logograms in Asian languages, or input from speech recognition processors.

features.name: Content Security Policy (CSP)
features.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) helps to mitigate certain security threats, including cross-site scripting (XSS) and clickjacking attacks. It consists of a set of directives from a website to a browser, which instruct the browser to restrict the things that the site is allowed to do.

features.name: Gradients
features.description: The linear-gradient() and radial-gradient() CSS functions and their repeating counterparts create backgrounds that progress smoothly between multiple colors.

features.name: HTTP Strict Transport Security
features.description: The Strict-Transport-Security HTTP response header informs browsers that the site should only be accessed using HTTPS, and that any future attempts to access it using HTTP should automatically be converted to HTTPS. Also known as HSTS.

features.name: Iterators and the for...of loop
features.description: The for...of loop operates on a sequence of values sourced from an iterable object, such as arrays, array-like objects, DOM collections, iterators, generators, and user-defined iterables. All built-in iterators inherit from the Iterator class.

features.name: Map (initial support)
features.description: Map objects hold key-value pairs and remember the original insertion order of the keys.

features.name: mask-type
features.description: The mask-type CSS property on an SVG <mask> element sets whether the mask is a luminance or alpha mask.

features.name: MutationObserver
features.description: The MutationObserver API watches for changes to the DOM tree and calls a callback function when DOM changes occur.

features.name: OES_element_index_uint WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_element_index_uint extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds support for gl.UNSIGNED_INT types to WebGLRenderingContext.drawElements().

features.name: OES_standard_derivatives WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_standard_derivatives extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds the GLSL derivative functions dFdx, dFdy, and fwidth.

features.name: OES_texture_float WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_float extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds floating-point pixel types for textures.

features.name: OES_texture_float_linear WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_float_linear extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts adds linear filtering with floating-point pixel types for textures.

features.name: OES_texture_half_float WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_half_float extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds texture formats with 16-bit (also known as half float) and 32-bit floating-point components.

features.name: OES_texture_half_float_linear WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_texture_half_float_linear extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds linear filtering with half floating-point pixel types for textures.

features.name: overflow-wrap
features.description: The overflow-wrap CSS property breaks a line of text onto multiple lines inside the targeted element in an otherwise unbreakable place to prevent overflow. The legacy property is word-wrap.

features.name: Page visibility
features.description: The document.visibilityState and document.hidden properties tell you whether the page is visible to the user (for example, it's not minimized or in a background tab).

features.name: Performance
features.description: The performance global object and the PerformanceObserver API provide access to performance-related information for the current execution context.

features.name: Promise (initial support)
features.description: A promise represents an asynchronous operation which eventually succeeds or fails.

features.name: requestAnimationFrame()
features.description: The requestAnimationFrame() method schedules a function that runs before the next repaint. You can use it to animate content with JavaScript.

features.name: Set (initial support)
features.description: Set objects store unique values of any type.

features.name: Sourcemap header
features.description: The Sourcemap HTTP response header links generated code to a source map, so the browser shows the original source in a debugger. This makes it easier to work with minified or transpiled code.

features.name: Speech synthesis
features.description: The SpeechSynthesis API converts text to speech with artificial voices.

features.name: URL
features.description: A URL object represents a web address, like https://example.com/, and parts of the address, such as the domain, path, and query string (as URLSearchParams).

features.name: Viewport units
features.description: The vw, vh, vmin, and vmax CSS viewport units are relative to the size of the viewport, and are used to size elements in relation to the viewport's dimensions.

features.name: WeakMap
features.description: A WeakMap object holds key-value pairs that do not create strong references to its keys, such that value data can be associated with a key without preventing garbage collection of the key.

features.name: WebGL
features.description: The WebGLRenderingContext API is the "webgl" rendering context for the <canvas> element. It represents a space for drawing two- and three-dimensional graphics and animations.

features.name: WEBGL_depth_texture WebGL extension
features.description: The WEBGL_depth_texture extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts defines 2D depth and depth-stencil textures.

features.name: WEBGL_lose_context WebGL extension
features.description: The WEBGL_lose_context extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts simulates losing and restoring a WebGLRenderingContext or WebGL2RenderingContext.

features.name: WebVTT
features.description: WebVTT is a captions and subtitles format. WebVTT files are loaded using the <track> element, and the VTTCue API can be used to create or update cues dynamically.

features.name: WebVTT cue settings
features.description: The VTTCue API updates various aspects of cues dynamically, such as alignment, size and position.

features.name: @supports
features.description: The @supports at-rule applies styles based on a browser's support for CSS features, such as a CSS property and value. Also known as feature queries.

features.name: 2D transforms
features.description: The transform CSS property and its 2D transform functions allow rotating, scaling, skewing, and translating an element. Arbitrary 2D transforms are also possible using a transformation matrix.

features.name: CSS object model
features.description: The CSS object model API reads, creates, and modifies CSS stylesheets and inline styles. Also known as CSSOM.

features.name: Date and time <input> types
features.description: The <input type="date"> and <input type="time"> HTML elements show date and time pickers.

features.name: EXT_blend_minmax WebGL extension
features.description: The EXT_blend_minmax extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds two blend equations, the minimum and maximum color components of the source and destination colors.

features.name: EXT_shader_texture_lod WebGL extension
features.description: The EXT_shader_texture_lod extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts adds texture functions to the OpenGL ES Shading Language such that the shader writer explicitly controls the level of detail (LOD).

features.name: Flexbox
features.description: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout system, which places content either horizontally or vertically, with optional wrapping.

features.name: font-kerning
features.description: The font-kerning CSS property sets whether kerning data from a font is used to adjust the space between letters.

features.name: OES_vertex_array_object WebGL extension
features.description: The OES_vertex_array_object extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds vertex array objects (VAOs) which encapsulate vertex array states. These objects keep pointers to vertex data and names for different sets of vertex data.

features.name: spellcheck
features.description: The spellcheck global HTML attribute sets whether the browser may check an element for spelling errors.

features.name: String repeat()
features.description: The repeat() method of strings returns the original string repeated a number of times.

features.name: String startsWith() and endsWith()
features.description: The startsWith() and endsWith() methods of strings returns whether a search string appears at the beginning or end of the provided string.

features.name: Symbol
features.description: A Symbol value is a unique, non-enumerable primitive value used for encapsulation or information hiding. For example, a symbol can be a key of an object that can never collide with any other key.

features.name: Transitions (CSS)
features.description: The transition shorthand CSS property sets how changes to an element's styles may occur over time. Transitions can be applied to specific CSS properties, all properties, or none.

features.name: WeakSet
features.description: A WeakSet object stores unique values of any type without creating strong references to the values, such that membership in the set does not prevent garbage collection of the value.

features.name: Classes
features.description: Classes are an object-oriented syntax for JavaScript prototypes.

features.name: DOMParser
features.description: The DOMParser API parses XML or HTML source code from a string into a DOM Document.

features.name: EXT_sRGB WebGL extension
features.description: The EXT_sRGB extension for WebGL 1.0 contexts adds sRGB support to textures and framebuffer objects.

features.name: HTTP/2
features.description: The HTTP/2 protocol is a major revision of the HTTP network protocol, providing improved performance and efficiency by using a single TCP connection to send multiple streams of data at once.

features.name: Interaction media queries
features.description: The pointer, any-pointer, hover, and any-hover CSS media queries set styles based on the presence of pointing devices and their ability to hover over elements. For example, most smartphones match the (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse) media query.

features.name: isolation
features.description: The isolation CSS property creates a new stacking context, which impacts z-index ordering and blend modes.

features.name: mix-blend-mode
features.description: The mix-blend-mode CSS property blends an element's content with its background or parent elements using blend modes like multiply, difference, or color.

features.name: String codePointAt() and fromCodePoint()
features.description: The codePointAt() method returns the numeric value of the UTF-16 code point at an index of the string. The fromCodePoint() method returns a string created from one or more code points.

features.name: String includes()
features.description: The includes() method of strings returns whether a search string appears within the string.

features.name: String raw()
features.description: The String.raw() static method interpolates template literal substitutions, but ignores escape sequences. It is the tag function for template literals.

features.name: @font-face
features.description: The @font-face CSS at-rule creates a custom font-family value. The at-rule's descriptors set the font's name, source, and various display settings.

features.name: <meter>
features.description: The <meter> element represents a scalar value within a known range or a fractional value, typically shown as a progress bar.

features.name: <picture>
features.description: The <picture> element is used for art direction in responsive images, where a different image is displayed based on the <source> element.

features.name: all
features.description: The all CSS property is a shorthand for all CSS properties, except for direction and unicode-bidi. It accepts only the keywords for explicit defaulting (such as initial and inherit), since they are the only values supported on all CSS properties.

features.name: Animations (CSS)
features.description: The animation CSS property animates an element's style over time, using keyframes described in @keyframes rules.

features.name: Base64 encoding and decoding
features.description: The atob() and btoa() global functions encode and decode strings to and from base 64, respectively.

features.name: EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic WebGL extension
features.description: The EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts adds anisotropic filtering (AF). AF improves the quality of mipmapped texture access when viewing a textured primitive at an oblique angle.

features.name: Font loading
features.description: The document.fonts API dynamically loads custom fonts and tracks when fonts are loading or ready to use.

features.name: font-variant-ligatures
features.description: The font-variant-ligatures CSS property sets how characters can be visually combined for readability or stylistic reasons.

features.name: Gamepad
features.description: The navigator.getGamepads() API accesses and responds to signals from game controllers.

features.name: Generators
features.description: Generator functions (function*) create iterators that return multiple values, one after another, on-demand.

features.name: Intl
features.description: The Intl API provides language sensitive string comparison, number formatting, date and time formatting, and more.

features.name: object-fit
features.description: The object-fit CSS property sets how images, videos, and other replaced elements are scaled within their container.

features.name: object-position
features.description: The object-position CSS property places images, videos, and other replaced elements within their boxes.

features.name: srcset and sizes
features.description: The srcset and sizes attributes for elements set a list of possible sources for the image and a corresponding list of size conditions for choosing a source, to show a responsive image that fits the size of the display.

features.name: String normalize()
features.description: The normalize() method of strings returns a Unicode normal form of a string as a new string. More than one code point sequence can represent the same characters. You can use the normalize() method to find canonically or compatibly equivalent strings.

features.name: touch-action
features.description: The touch-action CSS property sets whether an element on a touch screen can be panned or pinched to zoom.

features.name: Unicode point escapes
features.description: Unicode point escapes (\\u{}) represent Unicode characters within strings.

features.name: User agent sniffing
features.description: The navigator.userAgent property and several others loosely identify a browser. Selectively showing content based on the user agent string, also known as user agent sniffing, is unreliable. Consider using feature detection or user agent client hints instead.

features.name: WEBGL_debug_renderer_info WebGL extension
features.description: The WEBGL_debug_renderer_info extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts exposes information about the graphics driver for debugging purposes.

features.name: will-change
features.description: The will-change CSS property gives hints to the browser about expected changes to an element's scroll position, contents, or style. These hints allow browsers to optimize for upcoming style changes.

features.name: with
features.description: The with JavaScript statement adds a given object to the chain of scopes used to evaluate names.

features.name: word-break
features.description: The word-break CSS property sets how lines break within words.

features.name: :indeterminate
features.description: The :indeterminate CSS pseudo-class selects any form element whose state is indeterminate, such as checkboxes that have been set to an indeterminate state with JavaScript, or radio buttons which are members of a group in which all radio buttons are unchecked.

features.name: Clipboard events
features.description: The "copy", "cut", and "paste" events fire on elements when the user starts an action with the clipboard.

features.name: Constraint validation API
features.description: Methods that validate form controls before submission, such as checkValidity(), reportValidity() and setCustomValidity().

features.name: File API
features.description: The File API represents and reads from file data and metadata. Typically, you get files through other APIs, such as the <input type="file"> element or drag-and-drop events. You may also send file data to other APIs, such as creating images or drawing on canvases.

features.name: Resource timing performance entries
features.description: A resource performance entry records when a network event happens while loading a resource, such as when a connection starts and ends. You can use this information to measure loading times.

features.name: shape-outside
features.description: The shape-outside CSS property, along with shape-margin and shape-image-threshold, sets the shape around which adjacent content will wrap.

features.name: shapes
features.description: The circle(), ellipse(), inset(), and polygon() CSS shape functions create shapes for use with clip-path and shape-outside.

features.name: Text encoding and decoding
features.description: The TextEncoder API transforms a stream of code points into a byte stream with UTF-8 encoding, and TextDecoder does the reverse.

features.name: unset
features.description: The unset keyword resets any CSS property, removing any values previously set by the author, user, or browser. Inherited properties (like color) reset to the parent element's computed value. Non-inherited properties (like display) reset to the specified initial value (inline).

features.name: Web Cryptography
features.description: The Web Cryptography API performs low-level cryptographic operations, such as encryption, decryption, and signature verification. Also known as the Web Crypto API.

features.name: :placeholder-shown
features.description: The :placeholder-shown CSS pseudo-element selects <input> and <textarea> elements when no value is set and the element's placeholder attribute is not empty. Not to be confused with ::placeholder, which selects the placeholder text itself.

features.name: <input type="range">
features.description: The <input type="range"> element represents a slider for choosing an inexact value between a minimum and maximum value.

features.name: Fetch
features.description: The fetch() method makes asynchronous HTTP requests.

features.name: Mixed content handling
features.description: When a document is loaded over HTTPS, browsers ensure that none of the document's resources are loaded over an insecure protocol. Instead, resources that the document attempts to load over an insecure protocol are either loaded over HTTPS or are blocked.

features.name: Array copyWithin()
features.description: The copyWithin() method of arrays and typed arrays shifts or copies items of an array to another index of the array without changing its length.

features.name: Array fill()
features.description: The fill() method of arrays and typed arrays sets all or some items of an array to a given a value.

features.name: Array find() and findIndex()
features.description: The find() and findIndex() methods of arrays and typed arrays search an array for the first item that satisfies a test function.

features.name: Array.from()
features.description: The Array.from() and typed array .from() static methods copy items from an iterable or array-like object to make a new array.

features.name: Array.of()
features.description: The Array.of() and typed array .of() static methods create new arrays from the values of any number of arguments.

features.name: Case-insensitive attribute selector
features.description: The i identifier in a CSS attribute selector matches attribute values case-insensitively in document languages like XML where attribute values are case-sensitive.

features.name: image-rendering
features.description: The image-rendering CSS property sets how images are scaled, retaining smoothness for photos, or hard edges for pixel art and QR codes.

features.name: Typed array iteration methods
features.description: Typed array iteration methods

features.name: Typed array iterators
features.description: Typed arrays are iterable with the for … of statement and enumerable with the methods entries(), keys(), and values().

features.name: Upgrade insecure requests
features.description: The Upgrade-Insecure-Requests HTTP request header tells the server that the response should redirect to a secure (HTTPS) resource.

features.name: Array includes()
features.description: The includes() method of arrays and typed arrays returns whether a given value appears in the array.

features.name: Beacons
features.description: The navigator.sendBeacon() method asynchronously sends an HTTP POST request with a limited amount of data, typically for app state, events, and analytics data. The one-way beacon is guaranteed to be initiated before the browser unloads the page, but the sender does not get to handle the response.

features.name: column-fill
features.description: The column-fill CSS property sets the distribution of content across columns in a multi-column layout.

features.name: column-span
features.description: The column-span CSS property controls whether a child element extends across all columns of a multi-column parent.

features.name: CSS.escape()
features.description: The CSS.escape() static method escapes a string so that it can be used in a valid CSS selector.

features.name: download
features.description: The download attribute for <a> elements loads the target URL as a file to be saved, instead of navigating to it. An optional attribute value sets a default file name.

features.name: font-feature-settings
features.description: The font-feature-settings CSS property sets low-level OpenType feature tags for a font. When possible, use font-variant instead.

features.name: Multi-column layout
features.description: Multi-column layout flows an element's content across one or more columns in a single row, without affecting the display property of its children.

features.name: background-blend-mode
features.description: The background-blend-mode CSS property blends an element's background image and background color using blend modes like multiply, difference, or color.

features.name: Custom properties
features.description: Custom properties are CSS properties prefixed with -- that set values you can reuse with the var() function. For example, you can set a --key-color property to reuse as border-color: var(--key-color). Also known as CSS variables.

features.name: document.elementFromPoint() and document.elementsFromPoint()
features.description: The document.elementFromPoint() and document.elementsFromPoint() methods find the top-most element at a given point in the viewport, or all elements at a given point in the viewport, respectively.

features.name: document.write()
features.description: The document.open(), document.write(), document.writeln(), and document.close() methods write content to a document, possibly while that document is still loading.

features.name: Let and const
features.description: The let and const declarations define block-scoped variables.

features.name: Proxy and Reflect
features.description: The Proxy and Reflect JavaScript built-ins intercept and define custom behavior for fundamental language operations (such as property lookup, assignment, enumeration, or function invocation).

features.name: text-underline-position
features.description: The text-underline-position CSS property sets the position of underlines on text. For example, text-underline-position: under places the underline below the text, avoiding crossing descenders. The underline may be further adjusted by the text-underline-offset property.

features.name: writing-mode
features.description: The writing-mode CSS property sets whether text is laid out horizontally or vertically, and left to right, or right to left.

features.name: writing-mode SVG 1.1 values
features.description: The lr, lr-tb, rl, rl-tb, tb, and tb-rl keyword values for the writing-mode CSS property set the text direction for elements in SVG 1.1 documents.

features.name: Encrypted media extensions
features.description: The mediaKeys property of HTMLMediaElement and the navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess() method control the playback of content subject to digital rights management. Also known as EME.

features.name: Layout direction override
features.description: The unicode-bidi and direction CSS properties override the Unicode layout algorithm. They are intended for Document Type Definition (DTD) designers. For HTML documents, you should use the dir global HTML attribute and <bdo> HTML element instead.

features.name: min-content and max-content
features.description: The min-content and max-content CSS keywords represent the smallest and largest intrinsic sizes of an element.

features.name: Page breaks
features.description: In printed page layouts, the break-after, break-before, break-inside CSS properties control where printed pages start and end. Also known as pagination or page breaking.

features.name: Service workers
features.description: The service worker of a website is a script that runs in its own thread and which acts as local proxy that intercepts network requests from the website. Use a service worker to implement advanced caching strategies, offline support, background tasks, or push notification support on your website.

features.name: Subresource integrity
features.description: Subresource integrity verifies that a resource, such as script served from a content delivery network, matches a known cryptographic hash. Also known as SRI.

features.name: <link rel="preconnect">
features.description: The rel="preconnect" attribute for the <link> HTML element is a hint to the browser that the page or user is likely to request resources from another origin, so the browser should preemptively start a connection to the href value's origin.

features.name: Brotli compression
features.description: Brotli is a lossless data compression algorithm. When used as a content encoding, it often provides better compression than gzip.

features.name: Exponentiation operator
features.description: The exponentiation (**) operator returns the result of raising the first operand to the power of the second operand.

features.name: fit-content
features.description: The fit-content CSS keyword expands a box as needed to fit its contents until the maximum size is reached, preserving the content's preferred aspect ratio.

features.name: font-variant-caps
features.description: The font-variant-caps CSS property sets whether text should be displayed in small caps, petite caps, or with capital letters designed for titles.

features.name: font-variant-numeric
features.description: The font-variant-numeric CSS property sets how numeric characters are displayed. For example, you can align columns of numbers or use zeroes that have a slash.

features.name: WEBGL_compressed_texture_astc WebGL extension
features.description: The WEBGL_compressed_texture_astc extension for WebGL 1.0 and 2.0 contexts adds the Adaptive Scalable Texture Compression format to compressedTexImage2D() and compressedTexSubImage2D().

features.name: captureStream() for <canvas>
features.description: The captureStream() method for <canvas> elements returns a MediaStream which includes a CanvasCaptureMediaStreamTrack representing real-time video of the canvas image. You can use this to record the canvas, or send it elsewhere, such as another canvas or WebRTC connection.

features.name: filter
features.description: The filter CSS property applies one or more graphic effects to an element. You can use filter functions, such as blur() and drop-shadow(), alone or combined to produce different effects. For instance, filter: blur(2px).

features.name: translate
features.description: The translate HTML attribute marks whether an element's text should be translated.

features.name: <slot>
features.description: The <slot> HTML element is a placeholder inside a web component where consumers of the component can insert their own markup.

features.name: Border images
features.description: The border-image CSS property draws an image around an element.

features.name: dirname
features.description: The dirname attribute of <textarea> and <input> HTML elements includes the field's writing direction as form data on submission.

features.name: PNG
features.description: The PNG (Portable Network Graphics) image format is a raster graphics file format with animation, alpha transparency, and lossless compression.

features.name: Shadow DOM
features.description: Shadow DOM allows you to attach encapsulated "shadow" DOM trees to elements. A shadow DOM tree is a separate component, isolated from the scripts and styles in other parts of the document. This is a part of Web Components.

features.name: <link rel="preload">
features.description: The rel="preload" attribute for the <link> HTML element requests resources, such as images or style sheets, that the page needs soon, so the browser may prioritize them for loading before rendering begins.

features.name: Async functions
